question.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle. The ratio of the length of a side of the hexagon to the length of the shorter of the arcs intercepted by the side is:

solutions.explanation:
Let the circle have radius \(r>0\). Joining its center to the six vertices divides the full turn into six equal central angles, each
\[
\frac{360^\circ}{6}=60^\circ.
\]
The triangle formed by two adjacent radii and a hexagon side is isosceles. Its remaining angles are also \(60^\circ\), so it is equilateral and the side length is \(r\).

The intercepted shorter arc has central angle \(60^\circ<180^\circ\), so its length is one-sixth of the circumference:
\[
\frac16(2\pi r)=\frac{\pi r}{3}.
\]
Thus the requested ratio is
\[
r:\frac{\pi r}{3}=\boxed{3:\pi},
\]
choice D.
solutions.title: Compare a radius with one-sixth of the circumference
